arxiv-2209-08030.title: Detection of Interacting Variables for Generalized Linear Models via Neural Networks
arxiv-2209-08030.creator: Yevhen Havrylenko, Julia Heger
arxiv-2209-08030.description: Abstract The quality of generalized linear models (GLMs), frequently used by insurance companies, depends on the choice of interacting variables. The search for interactions is time-consuming, especially for data sets with a large number of variables, depends much on expert judgement of actuaries, and often relies on visual performance indicators.

arxiv-2301-01667.title: Learning-based MPC from Big Data Using Reinforcement Learning This research was funded by the Research Council of Norway (RCN) through the project Safe Reinforcement Learning using MPC (SARLEM), grant number 300172.
arxiv-2301-01667.creator: Shambhuraj Sawant, Akhil S Anand, Dirk Reinhardt, Sebastien Gros
arxiv-2301-01667.description: Abstract This paper presents an approach for learning Model Predictive Control (MPC) schemes directly from data using Reinforcement Learning (RL) methods. The state-of-the-art learning methods use RL to improve the performance of parameterized MPC schemes. However, these learning algorithms are often gradient-based methods that require frequent evaluations of computationally expensive MPC schemes, thereby restricting their use on big datasets.

arxiv-2412-05479.title: LATTE : Learning to Think with Vision Specialists
arxiv-2412-05479.creator: Zixian Ma, Jianguo Zhang, Zhiwei Liu, Jieyu Zhang, Juntao Tan, Manli Shu, Juan Carlos Niebles, Shelby Heinecke, Huan Wang, Caiming Xiong, Ranjay Krishna, Silvio Savarese
arxiv-2412-05479.description: Abstract While open-source vision-language models perform well on simple question-answering, they still struggle with complex questions that require both perceptual and reasoning capabilities. We propose LATTE , a family of vision-language models that have LeArned to Think wiTh vision spEcialists.

arxiv-2509-24387.title: AdaNav: Adaptive Reasoning with Uncertainty for Vision-Language Navigation
arxiv-2509-24387.creator: Xin Ding, Jianyu Wei, Yifan Yang, Shiqi Jiang, Qianxi Zhang, Fucheng Jia, Liang Mi, Yuxuan Yan, Weijun Wang, Yunxin Liu, Zhibo Chen, Ting Cao
arxiv-2509-24387.description: Abstract Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires agents to follow natural language instructions by grounding them in sequential visual observations over long horizons. Explicit reasoning could enhance temporal consistency and perception–action alignment, but reasoning at fixed steps often leads to suboptimal performance and unnecessary computation. To address this, we propose AdaNav , an uncertainty-based adaptive reasoning framework for VLN.

pmc-11490600.title: Bandgap formation mechanism in tacticity inspired elastic mechanical metastructures
pmc-11490600.creator: Ankur Dwivedi, Rajendra Kumar Munian, Bishakh Bhattacharya, Sondipon Adhikari
pmc-11490600.description: Tacticity is long known as a significant contributor in changing the chemical and mechanical properties of the polymers drastically. This study explores mechanism of bandgap formation in elastic mechanical metastructures designed with a focus on tacticity. We introduce metabeams, comprising a primary slender beam embedded with short secondary beams featuring end masses at their tips.

pmc-11595781.title: Isolation of Candida Species Is Associated with Comorbidities, Prolonged Mechanical Ventilation, and Treatment Outcomes in Surgical ICU Patients, a Cross-Sectional Study

pmc-11595781.description: The isolation of Candida may be related to comorbidity, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and survival during intensive care unit (ICU) stay, especially with non-albicans Candida (NAC). To examine the frequency of Candida isolation, associated comorbidities and outcomes in the surgical ICU in Osijek University Hospital, Croatia, the data from the electronic database from May 2016 to 30 June 2023 were analyzed.

pmc-13469945.title: Hidden in plain sight: Chlorhexidine as the culprit in recurrent perioperative anaphylaxis
pmc-13469945.creator: Josue A. Valdez, Emily Gansert, Victoria Hough, Alexei Gonzalez-Estrada
pmc-13469945.description: A 37-year-old renal transplant candidate experienced recurrent perioperative anaphylaxis during induction. Skin testing during a comprehensive allergy evaluation identified chlorhexidine allergy. After chlorhexidine avoidance and use of povidone iodine, the patient subsequently underwent successful renal transplantation without complications. Perioperative anaphylaxis (POA) has an incidence of approximately 1 in 7000 procedures, with a mortality rate of 2% in the United States.
